event_daxia_chest_r0.why: 球球把秘笈攤開舉在胸前，畫著三個出招小貓的內頁整面朝觀眾，他看的是書背。
event_daxia_chest_r0.scene: SETTING, copied from reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event): the dark wooden staircase corner with its banister and round-topped newel post, on a small patch of dark wooden floorboards, and the SAME old wooden chest with dark iron corner plates, one big paw print carved on its lid and an old iron padlock hanging sprung open from the hasp. The chest lid is now thrown wide open. On the floor beside the chest lie a few odds and ends that Qiuqiu has pushed out of the way: a folded old grey cloth, a small coil of rope and a dented tin cup. Qiuqiu KNEELS on the floor right beside the open chest, seen in three-quarter view, and reads a thick old stitched martial-arts manual that he has just lifted out of the bottom of the chest. He holds the OPEN book up in front of his chest with both paws, tilted toward his face: the open pages face HIM and his eyes look down into them, so the viewer sees only the OUTSIDE of the book - its plain worn dark-brown covers and spine, no writing, no pictures. None of the pages' drawings are visible to the viewer. Amazed, excited face: eyes wide and shining, mouth a little open.
refs: the setting of this same event to copy: the staircase corner with its banister and newel post, the wooden floorboards and the old iron-cornered chest with the carved paw print and the sprung-open padlock. Take only the setting and the chest, not Qiuqiu's pose.

event_sunbath_r1.why: 球球雙手橫拿卷軸在胸前，畫著飛踢小貓的那面朝觀眾，他低頭看的是背面；地上攤開的幾張卷軸也是正對觀眾、對他是倒的。
event_sunbath_r1.scene: SETTING, copied from reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event): a small patch of wooden floorboards in a corner with a low wooden plank wall and a small wooden window shutter standing slightly open; warm sunlight streams in through the gap and lays a bright yellow patch of light on the floor. Qiuqiu sits cross-legged right in the patch of sunlight, warm and relaxed, going over the moves he has learned. Beside him on the floor lie three small ROLLED-UP paper scrolls, each rolled shut and tied with a string. With both paws he holds one OPENED scroll up in front of his face: its drawn side faces HIM and his eyes look at it, so the viewer sees only the PLAIN BLANK BACK of the paper between its two wooden rollers - no drawing, no marks on the side facing the viewer. He frowns at it with a thoughtful, slightly fed-up face (lowered eyebrows, mouth a small flat line): this is the move that keeps going wrong.
refs: the setting of this same event to copy: the wooden floorboards, the low plank wall with the small window shutter standing slightly open and the bright patch of sunlight on the floor. Take only the setting, not Qiuqiu's pose.

event_pigeon_grandpa_r0.why: 念信給爺爺：畫柿子和紅蝴蝶結的信紙正面朝觀眾，球球看的是空白背面。
event_pigeon_grandpa_r0.scene: SETTING, copied from reference image 3 (another picture of this same event): the attic corner under sloping dark wooden roof beams, a hanging paper lantern with a paw print, a small round window showing the night sky and moon, stacks of old wooden crates and boxes, a patch of wooden floor with an open trapdoor. Qiuqiu sits on the floor right beside the OLD CAT, who looks EXACTLY as in reference image 3: a big grey-brown tabby with bushy white eyebrows, round wire-rimmed glasses, an olive-green patched coat and a grey scarf. Qiuqiu holds the letter - one single sheet of paper - up in front of him with both paws and reads it aloud, mouth open, speaking. The written side of the letter faces Qiuqiu and the old cat (both of them look at it), so the viewer sees only the PLAIN BLANK BACK of the sheet: no drawing, no marks on the side facing the viewer. The old cat sits leaning in at Qiuqiu's shoulder and laughs so hard that his round glasses sit crooked on his nose, tilted to one side; his eyes are squeezed shut with laughter and one paw holds his belly.
refs: the attic setting and the OLD CAT of this same event to copy exactly (grey-brown tabby, bushy white eyebrows, round glasses, olive-green patched coat, grey scarf). Take the attic and the old cat's look, not the poses, and no writing desk.

event_pigeon_reply_r1.why: 蠟筆畫（綁紅蝴蝶結的小貓）的畫面朝觀眾，球球低頭看的是背面。
event_pigeon_reply_r1.scene: SETTING, copied from reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event): the tower top at night - a patch of dark grey stone paving, a dark stone railing with round-topped posts, a big pale-yellow full moon behind. Sitting close beside him against the railing is the grey POSTMAN PIGEON exactly as in reference image 3 (grey feathers a little ruffled, NO cap, a brown satchel on a strap across its body); with both wings it hugs against its chest the small bundle wrapped in old beige cloth and tied with string, resting calmly beside Qiuqiu.
refs: the setting of this same event to copy (the stone paving, the dark stone railing, the big full moon), the grey postman pigeon's look (no cap, brown satchel) and the small bundle of old beige cloth tied with string. Take only the setting, the pigeon's look and the bundle, not the poses, not the flag and not the lantern.

event_cell_bandit_r0.why: 欠條蓋紅爪印那面朝觀眾，球球眼睛看畫面外；文字是他低頭一看，發現保證人欄蓋著小小的貓爪印。
event_cell_bandit_r0.scene: SETTING, copied from reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event): the dungeon cell on a patch of stone floor with some rubble - rusty iron bars with the cell door now swung OPEN, an old rusty padlock hanging open from the door, a rough stone wall with a lit wall torch and a map scratched into the stone. The TABBY BANDIT, looking exactly as in reference image 3 (a grey tabby cat with dark stripes, a bandage plaster on his face, a broken iron chain hanging around his neck, a torn brown vest), has just burst out of the open cell; he grins widely and throws one arm around Qiuqiu's shoulders in a big hug. Qiuqiu stands beside him and looks DOWN at the crumpled IOU paper the bandit has just stuffed into his paws: he holds the paper in both paws in front of his chest, tilted up toward his face, and its written side faces QIUQIU, so the viewer sees only the plain blank back of the crumpled sheet - no red print, no marks on the side facing the viewer. His eyes look down at the paper. Qiuqiu's face: shocked and dismayed, eyes wide, mouth open, one small sweat drop - he has just found out he is the guarantor.
refs: the setting of this same event to copy (iron bars and cell door with the rusty padlock, the stone wall with the wall torch and the scratched map) and the tabby bandit's look (grey tabby, face plaster, broken chain around the neck, torn brown vest). Take the setting and the bandit's look, not the poses.

event_rare_catnip_master_r0.why: 舊紙畫著好幾隻出爪大貓的那面朝觀眾，球球看的是背面；文字是紙上只畫一隻大貓一招一式地出爪、最後一格手腕往下壓半寸，球球跪在窩裡照著比。
event_rare_catnip_master_r0.scene: SETTING, copied from reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event): the stone terrace at the tower top - a big round bed of green catnip with small white flowers on a low stone-edged platform, a low dark stone railing, a glowing stone lantern, a big pale full moon behind. In the middle of the catnip is a large flattened cat-shaped hollow of pressed-down grass with a small tuft of grey fur with dark stripes in it; the orange gourd with its red cord lies tipped over at the edge of the field. Qiuqiu KNEELS inside the flattened hollow in the FOREGROUND, seen in a three-quarter back view from behind and slightly to the left: we see his back, his ringed tail and the back of his head with the two headband tails, his face turned in profile. The old sheet of paper lies unfolded FLAT on the pressed grass directly BEYOND him - further from the viewer than Qiuqiu, higher up in the picture, a little to the right of his head so his body does not hide it - so its drawings are the right way up both for Qiuqiu and for the viewer. On the paper there are only simple ink drawings of ONE and the same big cat, drawn three times in a row from left to right, doing one claw strike step by step; in the last drawing the big cat's wrist is pressed slightly DOWN, marked with one tiny downward arrow next to the wrist (ink pictures only, no letters, no writing, no other cats). Qiuqiu copies it from his knees, facing the paper: one paw thrust forward in a claw strike with the wrist bent slightly down, the other paw pulled back at his side, his eyes on the paper, a concentrated face and one small sweat drop.
refs: the setting of this same event to copy: the catnip bed with white flowers, the stone railing, the stone lantern, the moon, the flattened cat-shaped hollow with the grey striped fur tuft, and the orange gourd with its red cord. Take only the setting, not Qiuqiu's pose and not the small paper in that picture.

event_rat_bathhouse_r0.why: 在木桶裡泡澡還綁著深藍頭巾。泡澡要取下頭巾、脫衣（放在一旁）。
event_rat_bathhouse_r0.scene: SETTING, copied from reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event): the small stone bathhouse corner - a stone archway with a hanging wooden sign carved with a simple hot-spring steam symbol (a picture, no letters), a wall torch, wooden shelves piled with travellers' bags, a wooden counter, and round wooden bathtubs with white steam rising. Qiuqiu soaks in one big round wooden bathtub full of hot water, only his head and shoulders showing above the rim, steam rising around him. A small folded white towel sits on top of his head. Blissful, melted face, both eyes closed in happy curves. His head is BARE - NO headband anywhere on his head or around his neck; the grey-brown stripes on the top of his head show. In the tub he wears NOTHING: no gi, no collar showing; his shoulders and paws are bare cream fur, his paws resting on the tub rim. Right BESIDE the tub stands a small wooden stool; on it lie his navy headband folded neatly with its two tails hanging over the edge, and his navy ninja gi and black sash folded in a neat pile. To the side, the grey MOUSE KEEPER with big pink ears stands at the wooden counter with Qiuqiu's navy travel bag open on top of it, secretly rummaging through it.
refs: the setting of this same event to copy: the stone archway with the hanging wooden steam-symbol sign, the wall torch, the shelves of bags, the wooden counter, the wooden bathtubs, and the grey mouse keeper with big pink ears. Take the setting and the mouse's look, not the poses.
event_rat_bathhouse_r0.gear_off: this picture is the ONE EXCEPTION to the worn-gear rule: Qiuqiu is bathing, so his navy headband is taken OFF and lies folded on the small wooden stool beside the tub, together with his folded navy gi and black sash; in the water his head is bare (nothing tied on it, only a small white towel resting on top) and his shoulders are bare fur - he wears nothing.

event_rare_hot_spring_r1.why: 慢慢滑進溫泉泡到胸口，卻還綁著頭巾、水面露出深藍忍者服的衣領和袖子。泡澡要脫衣、取下頭巾放岸邊。
event_rare_hot_spring_r1.scene: SETTING, copied from reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event): the hot spring pool among grey mossy rocks, a rough stone wall behind with a hanging wooden board carved with a cat bathing with squinting eyes, a bamboo spout pouring water into the pool, a small wooden bucket, a paper lantern with a paw print hanging from a wooden post, white steam rising, a few leaves floating on the water. At the pool edge stands a short wooden stake; Qiuqiu's brown travel bag hangs from it, its strap looped over the top of the stake, well away from the water. Qiuqiu has slid slowly into the hot water and soaks only up to his CHEST: his bare cream-furred upper chest, shoulders and arms show above the water, his forearms resting on the rock rim. Calm, relieved face with both eyes gently closed and a small smile. His head is BARE - NO headband anywhere; the grey-brown stripes on top of his head show - and he wears NOTHING: no gi, no collar, no sleeves. On a flat rock at the pool edge next to the stake lie his navy headband folded neatly with its two tails and his navy ninja gi and black sash folded in a neat pile. Thin wisps of purple smoke drift up off the fur on his head and shoulders and fade away into the white steam.
refs: the setting of this same event to copy: the rock pool, the stone wall with the carved bathing-cat board, the bamboo spout, the wooden bucket and the paw-print lantern on its post. Take only the setting, not Qiuqiu's pose.
event_rare_hot_spring_r1.gear_off: this picture is the ONE EXCEPTION to the worn-gear rule: Qiuqiu is bathing, so his navy headband is taken OFF and lies folded on a flat rock at the pool edge, next to his folded navy gi and black sash; in the water his head is bare (nothing tied on it) and his chest, shoulders and arms are bare fur - he wears nothing.

event_fallen_star_r0.why: 文字是球球用頭巾包著手把星星撿起來；圖裡是用一塊米色布包星星，頭巾還綁在頭上。應該是頭巾解下來纏在手上。
event_fallen_star_r0.scene: SETTING, copied from reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event): the tower-top stone platform of dark blue-grey paving stones with a low dark stone railing, a small scorched crater in the paving, the old brass armillary sphere star-machine lying toppled over on its side, and in the sky above a small constellation of gold stars joined by thin gold lines with one corner missing (a small dotted empty circle where a star is gone). Qiuqiu has UNTIED his navy headband from his head and wound it several times around his right paw like an oven mitt; with that wrapped paw he has just picked up the fallen star: a glowing golden star-shaped stone, steaming hot, sitting in his navy-wrapped paw. The star is too hot for him: he is about to toss it over to his other paw, his left paw held open and ready right next to it; small puffs of steam and little heat lines rise from the star. Pained, scrunched face with gritted teeth and one sweat drop (both eyes squeezed shut the same way). His head is BARE - nothing tied on it, the grey-brown stripes on top of his head show; the navy headband is ONLY wound around his paw. He hops on one foot. No beige cloth, no rag - the only thing around his paw is the navy headband.
refs: the setting of this same event to copy: the dark stone platform and railing, the scorched crater, the toppled brass armillary sphere and the constellation with the missing corner. Take only the setting and the star's look, not Qiuqiu's pose.
event_fallen_star_r0.gear_off: this picture is the ONE EXCEPTION to the worn-gear rule: Qiuqiu has untied his navy headband and wound it around his right paw like an oven mitt to hold the hot star; nothing is tied on his head.
